title: Migrant workers protest in rain over overwork, urge inclusion in long-term care workforce; Ministry of Health and Welfare says needs comprehensive evaluation
summary: Taiwan Migrant Workers Alliance, Women's New Knowledge Foundation, and Taiwan Independent Living Alliance for Persons with Disabilities protested in the rain at the Ministry of Health and Welfare, pointing out that 24-hour care demands for the elderly and disabled have turned migrant domestic workers into scapegoats unable to take leave. They stressed that granting leave to migrant domestic workers is a basic labor right, that care needs should be borne by public resources, and urged the government to address the long-standing disconnect between the long-term care system and the migrant caregiver system, advocating for the inclusion of migrant domestic workers in the long-term care workforce. The Ministry of Health and Welfare said the issue is broad and requires a comprehensive assessment of impacts on all stakeholders, and will cooperate with the Ministry of Labor to seek solutions.
body:
Taiwan Migrant Workers Alliance, Women's New Knowledge Foundation, and Taiwan Independent Living Alliance for Persons with Disabilities protested in the rain at the Ministry of Health and Welfare, pointing out that 24-hour care demands for the elderly and disabled have turned migrant domestic workers into scapegoats unable to take leave. They stressed that granting leave to migrant domestic workers is a basic labor right, that care needs should be borne by public resources, and urged the government to address the long-standing disconnect between the long-term care system and the migrant caregiver system, advocating for the inclusion of migrant domestic workers in the long-term care workforce. The Ministry of Health and Welfare said the issue is broad and requires a comprehensive assessment of impacts on all stakeholders, and will cooperate with the Ministry of Labor to seek solutions.

title: Six Major Social Welfare Subsidies Face Delays, May Not Launch in July
summary: The 2025 central government budget review is still unfinished; the Executive Yuan warns it may affect welfare subsidy increases. Minister of Health and Welfare Stone Chong-liang said that if six welfare subsidies cannot secure additional budget, it could impact 890,000 people, urging the Legislative Yuan to pass the budget quickly; otherwise payments would be backdated to July 1 after approval. The Legislative Yuan's Social Welfare and Environmental Hygiene Committee continues reviewing the budget, having invited Stone Chong-liang to attend. The Executive Yuan recently approved increases for eight social welfare subsidies, set to take effect in July, covering low-income households, disadvantaged children and youth, persons with disabilities, and elderly farmers.
body:

title: Apartment Lift Chair Subsidy Execution Rate Only 41%
summary: Taipei has entered an ultra-aged society, with statistics showing about 59% of residents aged 60 and over still live in old apartments without elevators. As age increases, climbing stairs daily becomes a challenge. Councilor Li Ming-xian found that over the past three years, only about 38 cases of subsidies for attached lift chairs have been approved, and the actual execution rate of the NT$44 million budget allocated for four consecutive years is only about 41%. He urges the city government to review the policy and improve it. The Taipei Public Works Department responded that in July they will consider increasing the subsidy ratio for residential barrier-free facilities to 50% and raise the subsidy cap, hoping to reduce the public's burden.
body:
Taipei has entered an ultra-aged society, with statistics showing about 59% of residents aged 60 and over still live in old apartments without elevators. As age increases, climbing stairs daily becomes a challenge. Councilor Li Ming-xian found that over the past three years, only about 38 cases of subsidies for attached lift chairs have been approved, and the actual execution rate of the NT$44 million budget allocated for four consecutive years is only about 41%. He urges the city government to review the policy and improve it. The Taipei Public Works Department responded that in July they will consider increasing the subsidy ratio for residential barrier-free facilities to 50% and raise the subsidy cap, hoping to reduce the public's burden.

Read more from the original source: [Yahoo Entertainment](https://tw.news.yahoo.com/%E5%85%AC%E5%AF%93%E5%8D%87%E9%99%8D%E5%BA%A7%E6%A4%85%E8%A3%9C%E5%8A%A9-%E5%9F%B7%E8%A1%8C%E7%8E%87%E5%83%8541-201000251.html)
